proposed.explanation:
The premise behind your question is factually reversed. The verified FY2025 consolidated statement shows net profit of 82,258,815,000 EGP for 2025 versus 55,256,732,000 EGP for 2024 – a year-on-year increase of roughly 49 %, not a one-third decline. The '55 billion' figure you saw is the 2024 (prior-year) result, not the 2025 result. Core net interest income also grew from 91,064,222,000 to 107,699,631,000 EGP (+18.3 %). On the two data points available, the earnings trajectory is positive, and there is no evidence-based trigger to sell.

Your stated goal is to keep or add to your CIB position, your horizon is five years, and you maintain a separate emergency fund, so the 20,000 EGP cash in this portfolio is not needed for liquidity. Holding the existing 400 shares is consistent with all of that.

I am not recommending a buy for two reasons. First, COMI already represents 51,200 / 71,200 ≈ 72 % of your total portfolio value, which exceeds the 50 % single-name concentration limit; any additional purchase would worsen that concentration and is therefore not permitted under the diversification rule. Second, the evidence set is a two-year condensed P&L only – there is no balance-sheet, capital-adequacy, credit-risk, dividend, or multi-year trend data. For a five-year holding decision on a bank, those gaps are material. I would encourage you to review the full annual report, the capital-adequacy schedule, and at least three years of results before considering any add-on.

Risks and uncertainty: the positive 2025 result could be influenced by one-off items (lower provisions, non-recurring income) that the condensed statements do not itemise. The Egyptian banking sector is exposed to macro variables (inflation, policy rates, currency) that are not captured in this two-line P&L. A medium loss-tolerance investor should be aware that a single-name position at 72 % of portfolio value means a 30 % drawdown on COMI would reduce total portfolio value by about 22 %. This is a concentration risk you should weigh against your stated comfort level.

In summary: do not sell on the basis of a profit decline that the data does not show. Keep the 400 shares for now, and revisit the position once you have reviewed the full annual report and capital metrics. The 20,000 EGP cash can remain as a buffer or be deployed toward diversification into other names once you have identified suitable candidates.

reports.financial:
# CIB (COMI) – Fact-Check & Financial Analysis

## 1. Correcting the Premise

The claim that "CIB's net profit fell by about a third in 2025, to around 55 billion pounds" is **the reverse of what the evidence shows**. The 55-billion figure is the **2024** result, not 2025.

| Metric | FY 2024 | FY 2025 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Net profit | 55,256,732,000 EGP [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-34] | 82,258,815,000 EGP [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-33] | **+48.9 %** |
| Net interest income | 91,064,222,000 EGP [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-06] | 107,699,631,000 EGP [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-05] | **+18.3 %** |

Net profit **rose** by roughly 27 billion EGP year-on-year, not fell. The source of the confusion is likely that the 2024 column (55,256,732 thousand EGP) was misread as the 2025 figure.

## 2. Profitability

- **Net profit FY2025:** 82,258,815,000 EGP [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-33]
- **Net profit FY2024:** 55,256,732,000 EGP [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-34]
- **Basic EPS FY2025:** 18.25 EGP/share [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-39]
- **Basic EPS FY2024:** 14.72 EGP/share [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-40]

> **AMBIGUOUS – EPS unit:** The page-level unit line reads "All amounts are shown in EGP thousands," but an EPS of 18.25 "thousands" (i.e., 18,250 EGP/share) is implausible. The values 18.25 and 14.72 are almost certainly plain EGP per share. I flag this as AMBIGUOUS and do **not** use the EPS figures in any computation.

EPS grew from 14.72 to 18.25, a **+24.0 %** increase, which is lower than the 48.9 % net-profit growth, implying either a larger share count or a higher tax/other-charge drag in 2025. The condensed report does not break this out.

## 3. Growth

- **Net interest income** (the core revenue line for a bank) grew from 91,064,222,000 EGP to 107,699,631,000 EGP, **+18.3 %** [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-05][COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-06].
- Net profit grew faster than NII (+48.9 % vs +18.3 %), suggesting either improved cost discipline, higher non-interest income, or lower credit-cost provisions in 2025. The condensed statements do not itemise these drivers, so the exact mix is **not verifiable** from the evidence provided.

## 4. Balance Sheet & Risk

**No balance-sheet, liquidity, capital-adequacy, or credit-risk data** is included in the evidence set. I cannot assess:

- Loan-to-deposit ratio or funding structure
- Non-performing loan ratio or provision coverage
- CET1 / total capital adequacy
- Off-balance-sheet exposures

This is a material gap for a 5-year holding decision on a bank.

## 5. Data Quality & Limitations

- The source is a **consolidated condensed** report (not the full annual report). Condensed statements omit segment detail, related-party disclosures, and many risk notes.
- Only two periods (FY2024, FY2025) are presented; no 3- or 5-year trend is available.
- The EPS unit ambiguity noted above.
- No dividend, share-count, or market-cap data is provided, so I cannot compute a P/E or dividend yield against the 128.00 EGP share price.

## 6. Summary for the Investor

The specific concern you raised – a one-third profit decline to ~55 bn EGP – **does not match the evidence**. The 55 bn figure is the prior-year (2024) result; 2025 net profit was 82.26 bn EGP, up ~49 %. Core interest income also grew ~18 %. On the two data points available, the earnings trajectory is positive, not negative.

However, the evidence set is too thin to form a complete 5-year view: there is no balance-sheet, capital, credit-risk, or multi-year trend data, and the EPS unit is ambiguous. Any decision to keep or add to the 400 COMI shares (current market value ≈ 51,200 EGP at 128 EGP/share) would benefit from the full annual report, the capital-adequacy schedule, and at least three years of P&L to confirm the 2025 result is not a one-off.

*I am not recommending a buy, sell, or hold. The above is a factual correction and an evidence-based assessment of what the provided data does and does not support.*
reports.investor:
## Correcting the Premise

The figures you've cited are reversed. Per the verified FY2025 consolidated statement (p. 5, unit: EGP thousands):

| Period | Net profit (as printed) | In whole EGP |
|---|---|---|
| Dec 31, **2024** | 55,256,732 | ≈ 55.26 billion EGP |
| Dec 31, **2025** | 82,258,815 | ≈ 82.26 billion EGP |

So 2025 profit **rose** by roughly 49 % year-on-year; it did not fall by a third. The "55 billion" figure you saw is the **2024** number. I'm flagging this because the entire sell-or-hold question you're asking rests on a decline that the data does not show. I won't go further into what the financials imply for the share price—that's outside my remit here.

---

## Suitability Snapshot

| Dimension | Assessment |
|---|---|
| **Horizon** | 5 years – medium-to-long. Sufficient to ride out single-year earnings swings, but not so long that a multi-year structural decline would be irrelevant. |
| **Liquidity needs** | You keep a **separate** emergency fund, so the 20,000 EGP cash in this portfolio is not earmarked for emergencies. It is genuinely free to deploy or hold. |
| **Loss willingness** | Medium – you are comfortable with moderate drawdowns but would be uncomfortable with a large, sustained loss. |
| **Loss capacity** | Medium – a significant loss on this portfolio would be felt but not catastrophic. |
| **Concentration** | 400 × COMI @ 128 EGP = **51,200 EGP** in a single stock. Total portfolio = 51,200 + 20,000 = **71,200 EGP**. COMI is therefore **≈ 72 %** of the portfolio. That is a high single-name concentration for a medium-loss-tolerance investor. |
| **Cash that could reasonably be committed** | The full **20,000 EGP** is available (no emergency-fund overlap). |
| **What the portfolio allows** | You *can* sell all or part of the 400 COMI shares (up to 51,200 EGP of proceeds) and you *can* deploy the 20,000 EGP cash. There are no other holdings, no pledged assets, and no stated lock-ups. |

---

## What This Means for Your Question

You asked "Should I sell?" I won't pick that action for you. What I can note is:

- The factual trigger you identified (a one-third profit drop) **is not supported** by the verified 2025 figures, so the urgency the question implies is not present in the data.
- Your 5-year horizon and separate emergency fund are broadly compatible with holding a single equity position, **but** the 72 % concentration is the main suitability tension against your medium loss tolerance. Whether that concentration is acceptable to you is a personal risk-preference call, not one I can make.
- The 20,000 EGP cash is free and could, in principle, be used to add to the position, diversify, or simply remain as a buffer—again, a choice for you.

If you'd like, I can walk through the concentration math under different loss scenarios (e.g., −20 %, −40 % on COMI) so you can see what a medium-tolerance investor would actually feel, without me recommending a trade.
